# Lighting and MDL fixtures

The sixteen light stages use distinct architectural, sculptural and tabletop subjects with matte, metallic and translucent Preview Surface materials. They exercise rectangle, disk, cylinder, sphere, shaped spotlight, distant, animated and dome lights, color temperature and normalization, complete light-rig variants (`warmStudio`, `coolRim`, `nightNeon`), and environment variants (`day`, `night`, `dayRotated`). They also author a dome portal, mesh and volume light APIs, deprecated GeometryLight, light and shadow collections, and a cached light list. Those latter features require delegate-specific transport or linking support; the EXR dome or a separate key provides their visible illumination. The manifest requests no viewer-supplied environment or thumbnail camera light for these cases. The 64×32 Radiance RGBE maps and uncompressed linear OpenEXR map are original procedural assets with asymmetric bright areas. Native schema assertions establish the authored rig and resolved assets; they do not establish exact physical illumination or variant behavior. The current viewer approximates disk lights with rectangular area lights and cylinder lights with point lights. Plugin lights and filters require an external renderer-specific definition and are not represented.

The six MDL stages have MDL-only surface terminals and exercise the viewer's existing authored-input approximation for `OmniPBR`, its clearcoat and opacity variants, and `gltf_material`. The subjects include metal, clearcoat, color texture, normal texture, and cutout cases. The included `.mdl` files are intentionally minimal identity modules to resolve the source-asset identifiers: they are not implementations of NVIDIA's MDL material libraries and are not a reference for MDL compilation or physical rendering. Native Storm has no MDL renderer in this setup, so its images show geometric display-color fallback; browser material/texture checks are required for the approximation. OmniGlass is not included because the current approximation does not recognize it.

`native-validation.json` records stage opens, composition errors and authored feature assertions with OpenUSD 26.05. The sixteen light stages also pass this build's `usdchecker`. The VolumeLight card uses `scripts/render-volume-light-reference.py` to render the surrounding native scene with the VDB volume deactivated in a temporary layer, because this Storm build lacks a VDB plugin; the card does not show volume emission. Its six MDL checks report `MissingSourceTypeInRegistry` because the native installation has no MDL shader registry plugin; this is a verifier limitation and is not a successful MDL validation. All HDR, EXR, PNG, and minimal MDL dependencies are generated locally by the script and referenced by relative path.

Regenerate with:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/Users/herbst/OpenUSD-26.05-native/lib/python /usr/local/bin/python3 scripts/generate-lighting-mdl-fixtures.py
```

The torus meshes have analytic unit vertex normals on a 96×32 mesh, preserving smooth metal highlights. Their native Storm cards were recaptured. Distant sun also authors `UsdLuxShadowAPI` and an enabled/disabled `shadows` variant; both public viewers update actual shadow maps when it changes. Shadow color, distance/falloff and selective shadow-link collections remain separate renderer work.

The light catalog uses `scenePrimitiveLightIntensityScale: 1`: authored luminance is no longer multiplied by different brightness overrides for each fixture. The delegate converts sphere luminance to point-light intensity, distant luminance to illuminance using the angular diameter, and normalized emission using world-space surface area. Disk lights retain a rectangular LTC approximation with matching total power; cylinders retain an isotropic point approximation. Nonuniformly scaled spheres use an effective radius rather than an ellipsoidal emitter. Native Storm 26.05 uses older projected-area normalization and point approximations for area lights, so its thumbnails are not an exact photometric reference for modern UsdLux normalization. Its display transform also differs from Needle AgX.

Preview Surface `emissiveColor` remains scene-linear and can exceed 1. Beauty applies ambient occlusion to reflected light without dimming emission. Optional bloom is available in View settings for the Three viewer's Basic and Beauty modes; it processes the HDR composite before tone mapping and includes transparent surfaces and volumes.
